senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; preced. wds.) stranger, gentile. [In editions published under the censor’s supervision, our w. is frequently changed into עכו״ם, גּוֹי, כּוּשִׁי, כּוּתִי &c.] Ab. Zar. IV, 4 (51ᵇ; 52ᵇ; Mish. ed. עכו״ם).
units: <cite ref="Chullin 13b:4">Ḥull. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>נ׳ שבחוצה לארץ לאו עובדי ע״ז וכ׳</he> gentiles outside of Palestine are not to be considered as idolaters, they only continue their fathers’ customs.
<cite ref="Gittin 61a:5">Gitt. 61ᵃ</cite> <he>מפרנסין עניי נ׳ וכ׳</he> we must support the poor of the gentiles &c.; (Tosef. ib. V (III), 4 <he>גוים</he>).

<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 5:9">Gitt. V, 9</cite> (<cite ref="Gittin 61a">61ᵃ</cite>) <he>מספידין מתי נ׳ וכ׳</he> (Mish. ed. <he>עכו״ם</he>) we must lament for the dead of the gentiles &c.; a. v. fr.—Fem. <cite ref="N00847"><he>נָכְרִית</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Yevamot 3:7">Ib. III, 7</cite> <he>שלשה אחים … ואחד נשוי נ׳</he> in the case of three brothers, two of whom married two sisters, and one a stranger; a. fr.
